reason: The cited evidence directly supports all key premises: E1 and E3 state that strength arises from fluctuations in shear-fault energy and that HAMs cause wavy dislocation motion; E2 shows jerky motion and pinning at high local fault-energy sites; E4 and E5 confirm that SRO, controlled by processing, increases energy landscape ruggedness, activation barriers, and yield strength relative to a random solution. The representation of the evidence is accurate.
premises: Local shear-fault energy fluctuations, not the average value, govern strength in CCAs.
Short-range chemical ordering (SRO) creates hard atomic motifs (HAMs) that act as dislocation pinning sites.
Dislocations in CCAs with SRO exhibit wavy/jerky motion due to pinning at high local fault-energy sites.
Annealing temperature can control the degree of SRO and thus the magnitude of fault-energy fluctuations.
Increased SRO raises activation barriers and lattice friction, leading to higher yield strength compared to a random solid solution.
